t: Connected Components in the LCM Graph — Sieve + Union-Find
o: Nodes i and j are joined when lcm(nums[i], nums[j]) <= threshold. Any value exceeding threshold can never join anything (its lcm with anyone is at least itself), so it forms its own component. For values <= threshold (at most 2e5 distinct candidates), note that two numbers with common divisor g satisfy lcm <= a*b/g, but the clean sufficient-and-complete trick is: for each g from 1 to threshold, union all present multiples of g — any pair with lcm <= threshold shares some divisor g <= threshold and gets unioned transitively. Example 1: 2 and 4 union via g=2; 8, 9, 3 stay separate → 4 components. Example 2: 12 joins nothing new within threshold 10 → 2 components.
k: Values above threshold are isolated; for each g <= threshold, union all present multiples of g — harmonic-series enumeration costs O(threshold log threshold).

a.i: Map each value <= threshold to its node index. For every g, walk its multiples m = g, 2g, 3g, ... <= threshold and union all present ones together. Any edge implied by lcm <= threshold is captured because lcm(a,b) <= threshold implies some common divisor g = a/gcd... concretely g = gcd(a,b) divides both and g <= lcm(a,b) <= threshold, so both are multiples of g and get unioned.
s: Build pos[value] = node index for values <= threshold; initialize DSU over all n nodes.
For g = 1..threshold, iterate multiples and union each present multiple with the first present multiple of g.
Count distinct DSU roots over all nodes (isolated large values contribute their own roots).
a.t: O(threshold log threshold + n α(n)) — the divisor-sieve double loop is harmonic; DSU unions are near-constant amortized.
a.sp: O(n + threshold) for the DSU and the value-to-index map.

a.i: Directly test every pair: if lcm(a,b) = a/gcd(a,b)*b <= threshold, union them. Correct and simple, but O(n^2) pairs with a gcd each — fine for tiny inputs, hopeless at n = 1e5.
s: For each pair (i, j), compute g = gcd(nums[i], nums[j]).
If nums[i]/g * nums[j] <= threshold, union i and j.
Return the number of distinct roots.
a.t: O(n^2 log V) — all pairs with a Euclidean gcd each; only viable for small n.

w: Use the sieve approach in any real submission; the pairwise version is only for reasoning about correctness. Why the sieve is complete: if lcm(a,b) <= threshold then g = gcd(a,b) <= lcm(a,b) <= threshold and both a and b are multiples of g, so iteration g unions them. Pitfalls: forgetting that values > threshold are automatically isolated components (they still count toward the answer), and computing lcm as a*b/g with overflow (divide first). Follow-up: threshold up to 1e9 with few numbers (then factorize each number and union over shared prime powers).
